daily.title: COP31: Fossil fuels still missing from draft deal at UN climate summit
daily.summary: Countries are still deeply divided despite weeks of negotiations. Nations are now mulling over a new draft text that still doesn't mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming. DW has more.

daily.title: Nigeria: At least 24 dead after boat capsizes
daily.summary: The boat carrying mourners for a funeral overturned in southern Nigeria. It was the latest in a series of deadly boat accidents in the country.

daily.title: Getting rid of antibiotic resistance: Challenges and possible solutions
daily.summary: If antibiotics stop working, even the smallest infection can be fatal. The WHO expects millions of deaths over the next 25 years. Can the "One Health" approach help combat antibiotic resistance?

daily.title: Mexican special forces arrest drug kingpin 'Chapo Isidro'
daily.summary: The alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang and one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, known as "Chapo Isidro," was captured by the Mexican military following a raid and a shootout in the coastal state of Sinaloa.

daily.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
daily.summary: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

daily.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
daily.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

daily.title: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
daily.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

daily.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
daily.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

daily.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
daily.summary: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.

daily.title: Anthropic researcher uses AI to solve math's greatest riddle
daily.summary: The proposed breakthrough could reshape mathematical research, but still needs independent verification. It's the latest in a string of cases where AI has outpaced humans in solving famous maths problems.

daily.title: Germany news: Support for Ukraine military aid waning, survey shows
daily.summary: Nearly half of Germany's population wants to reduce military aid to Ukraine, a survey has found. Meanwhile, German consumers are set to pay more in energy bills next year due in part to the Iran war. DW has more.

daily.title: 'Killer robots' talks at UN end with no legally binding ban
daily.summary: Countries have agreed to extend discussions over controls on lethal autonomous weapons systems for two years.

daily.title: US judge jails Indian national in foiled Sikh separatist murder plot
daily.summary: New Delhi has denied any role in the plot to kill Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. Meanwhile, over 200 people have been hospitalized after consuming spurious liquor in Manipur state. DW has more.

daily.title: Man convicted of arson over deadly 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles
daily.summary: A 30-year-old man has been convicted of causing one of the most destructive wildfires in the history of Los Angeles. The verdict came after the case was retried.

daily.title: Three El Salvador soldiers die in explosives accident in Haiti
daily.summary: The soldiers were part of a Salvadoran military contingent deployed to the violence-ridden Caribbean nation last month to rescue four missing airmen. The deployment has widened into an operation against Haiti's gangs.

weekly.title: Brazil ex-President Jair Bolsonaro taken to hospital over abdominal pain
weekly.summary: Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized in Brasilia with intestinal obstruction. The former far-right Brazilian leader is receiving pain medications, his son Carlos said.

weekly.title: UK anti-migrant activist jailed for slashing Channel dinghy
weekly.summary: Daniel Thomas, known as "Danny Tommo," slashed a dinghy with a knife while a French rescue worker was on board. The incident was livestreamed to a large social media audience amid growing tensions over migrant crossings.

weekly.title: US judge approves Bayer's $7.25 billion cancer settlement
weekly.summary: Bayer could end years of costly lawsuits in the US over claims that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. Tens of thousands of people could now receive compensation, although some lawyers say the payments are too low.

weekly.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
weekly.summary: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

weekly.title: Repression against Iranian lawyers increases
weekly.summary: At least 135 lawyers in Iran have been subjected to repressive measures over the past year. UN experts warn that this seriously jeopardizes the right of those accused to trial in a constitutional court.

weekly.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
weekly.summary: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?

weekly.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
weekly.summary: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

weekly.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
weekly.summary: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?

weekly.title: Can German auto manufacturing recover after Mercedes and VW cuts?
weekly.summary: German automakers are pulling back on investments at home, sparking fresh anxiety about the auto sector's future. Some industry watchers think there is still a narrow window to stem the decline. But how?

weekly.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
weekly.summary: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.

weekly.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
weekly.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.

weekly.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
weekly.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

weekly.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
weekly.summary: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

weekly.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
weekly.summary: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?

weekly.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
weekly.summary: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.

weekly.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
weekly.summary: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?

weekly.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
weekly.summary: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

weekly.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
weekly.summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

weekly.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
weekly.summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

weekly.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
weekly.summary: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.

weekly.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
weekly.summary: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.

weekly.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
weekly.summary: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

weekly.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
weekly.summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

weekly.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
weekly.summary: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.

weekly.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
weekly.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

weekly.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
weekly.summary: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

weekly.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
weekly.summary: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

weekly.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
weekly.summary: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

weekly.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
weekly.summary: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

weekly.title: Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
weekly.summary: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

weekly.title: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
weekly.summary: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

weekly.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
weekly.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

weekly.title: Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
weekly.summary: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

weekly.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
weekly.summary: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

weekly.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
weekly.summary: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.

weekly.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
weekly.summary: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.

weekly.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
weekly.summary: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

weekly.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
weekly.summary: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.

weekly.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
weekly.summary: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.

weekly.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?
weekly.summary: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.

weekly.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
weekly.summary: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

weekly.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
weekly.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz, Söder aim to revisit electricity tax cut
weekly.summary: The Christian Democrats are in Munich, pushing to revive some tax relief that didn't make it into the budget after talks last week. And Manuela Schwesig faces a vote on a new term as regional leader. Follow DW.

weekly.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
weekly.summary: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?

weekly.title: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'
weekly.summary: Research suggests that students who aren't careful about how they use ChatGPT and other AI tools risk poorer academic outcomes. It's a huge challenge for teachers.

weekly.title: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?
weekly.summary: The German economy is growing again, albeit slightly. However, economists warn that without reforms, higher productivity and solid public finances, a loss of prosperity and growing debt threaten future generations.

weekly.title: Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
weekly.summary: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

weekly.title: Germany news: Germany holds national day of remembrance
weekly.summary: Events were held for "Volkstrauertag," a day commemorating victims of war and oppression. Meanwhile, experts said the country is headed for a budget crisis.
